messages:
jamal (PM): quick sync — customer Z is pushing for the low-latency 'fast-path' feature. Sales says it's tied to a renewal next quarter. do we pull ppl off SLO work?

alex (SRE): what's the ask exactly? is this a perf regression fix or a new endpoint with different p99 targets?

jamal (PM): it's a new streaming endpoint optimized for short prompts. they want p95 < 120ms for short requests. product thinks it's high impact.

maya (EngMgr): we already have the SLO refactor and KV-cache toil burn-down in the board. that work targets reducing token cost and pager noise. if we shift, timelines slip.

erin (CS): from CS: customer is willing to sign a 12m contract if we can show an internal perf plan within 2 weeks. they care about consistent tail latency more than absolute throughput.

alex (SRE): we should check current error budget & recent incidents. if we can afford a small scope change under error budget, maybe acceptable. otherwise feature will increase oncall load.

ops-bot: incident created #INC-2026-89 for elevated p99 in region-us-west (auto-detect).

jamal (PM): i ran a quick RICE for the ask: Reach=0.08 (targeted customer class), Impact=8, Confidence=0.6, Effort=5 => RICE ~7.7. doesn't scream 'highly prioritized' compared to SLO refactor which had RICE 12.

maya (EngMgr): thanks for the numbers. two proposals: 1) timebox a 2-week spike to validate feasibility (small team, no full swap), 2) full dev pull if spike proves low effort. keeps SLO work mostly on track.

alex (SRE): +1 to the spike. during spike we should capture perf budgets, add canary with stricter latency SLO, and measure KV-cache impact. also add an automatic fallback to current model variant if tail degrades.

erin (CS): can we use a tech-preview with customer, so they get partial assurances while we continue SLO work? they'd accept that as long as we document risks.

jamal (PM): sounds reasonable. can we set launch criteria? my suggestion: (a) p95 < 120ms for 72h canary, (b) <10% additional pager events during canary, (c) rollback plan + SLA note.

alex (SRE): agree. add 'no sustained error budget burn' as a criteria. if burn > 20% in 72h, automatic rollback.

maya (EngMgr): i'll allocate one engineer + an SRE buddy for the 2-week spike. won't touch the toil burn-down board except for documenting spillover.

jamal (PM): i'll update RICE with the spike as a check (Effort down if spike good). erin you ok to present the tech-preview plan to the customer?

erin (CS): yes, i'll draft a one-pager outlining canary expectations and known risks.

alex (SRE): one more ask: put the SLO refactor tickets into 'blocked-by-spike' so we can re-prioritize quickly after spike.

maya (EngMgr): done — i moved tickets and added a small contingency buffer to Q2 plan.

jamal (PM): thanks all. summary: 2-week spike, canary launch criteria set, SLO work stays mostly on track with contingency. follow-up check 2026-05-03 14:00 UTC.

ops-bot: reminder set for 1832504380 (follow-up sync).
